title: Build a Complete CSS Website
subtitle: Bring your CSS skills together in a real project
description: Build a responsive, accessible website while reviewing essential CSS concepts from Lessons 1–9 and learning professional styling techniques.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Build a Complete CSS Website: concepts and applied practice

blocks.title: Welcome to Your CSS Capstone
blocks.content: You have reached the final lesson of the CSS course. You will now combine the skills you have learned to build a complete website called Nova Studio. The website will include a navigation bar, hero section, service cards, a call-to-action area, and a footer. You will also learn useful professional techniques such as CSS custom properties, specificity, accessible focus styles, and consistent sizing. By the end, you should understand how separate CSS techniques work together in one project.

blocks.title: 1. Plan the Website
blocks.content: Before writing CSS, identify the website's structure. HTML provides the content and meaning; CSS controls its presentation. Our website will use semantic HTML elements, reusable classes, a consistent color system, Flexbox for navigation, Grid for service cards, and media queries for smaller screens. Planning first makes your code easier to maintain.

blocks.title: Lesson 1 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: What is the main purpose of CSS in a website?
options: To style and arrange HTML content
To replace HTML and define all page content
To store user accounts and passwords
blocks.explanation: CSS controls presentation, including colors, spacing, layout, typography, and responsive behavior. HTML provides the document structure.

blocks.title: Lesson 1 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: A heading exists in HTML, but you want it to appear larger and blue. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Delete the heading and create it with CSS
Use a CSS rule to style the existing heading
Use a media query to replace the HTML
Put the heading text inside a CSS comment
blocks.explanation: Keep the heading in HTML and use CSS to control its appearance. This separates content from presentation.

blocks.title: 2. Understand Selectors and Specificity
blocks.content: Selectors determine which elements receive a CSS rule. A class selector such as .service-card targets elements with that class. An element selector such as h1 targets all h1 elements. An ID selector such as #main targets the element with that ID. When several rules conflict, CSS uses the cascade, specificity, and source order to determine which declaration applies. Prefer reusable classes for most component styling instead of relying heavily on IDs or !important.

blocks.title: Lesson 2 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: Which selector targets every element whose class is service-card?
blocks.explanation: A period begins a class selector. A hash begins an ID selector, while an element selector uses the element name.

blocks.title: Lesson 2 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: A class rule and an element rule both set the same property on one element. Assuming normal declarations and no other competing rules, which usually has higher specificity?
options: The rule with the shorter property value
blocks.explanation: A class selector has greater specificity than a simple element selector. Other factors, including !important, cascade layers, and inline styles, can affect the final result.

blocks.title: 3. Create a Consistent Visual Style
blocks.content: A professional website uses a small, coordinated set of colors and border styles. CSS custom properties let you store reusable values in one place. For example, --color-primary can represent your main brand color. The var() function retrieves the value. If the brand color changes later, you can update the variable instead of searching through every rule.

blocks.title: Set Up Reusable Design Variables
blocks.output: Defines reusable dark-theme colors, surfaces, text colors, and card radius so the whole interface can change consistently.

blocks.title: Lesson 3 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: What does this declaration do: background: var(--color-primary);?
options: Uses the value stored in the --color-primary custom property
blocks.explanation: The var() function retrieves a CSS custom property's value so it can be reused in declarations.

blocks.title: Lesson 3 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: Which CSS property creates a rounded corner on a card?
blocks.explanation: border-radius rounds an element's corners. It can use pixel, percentage, and other valid CSS length values.

blocks.title: 4. Control Space with the Box Model
blocks.content: Every element has a box model: content, padding, border, and margin. Padding adds space inside the border; margin adds space outside it. The box-sizing property helps make dimensions predictable. With box-sizing: border-box, an element's declared width includes its padding and border. This makes sizing layouts easier to manage.

blocks.title: Use Predictable Sizing
blocks.output: Applies border-box sizing so padding and borders are included in an element’s declared width.

blocks.title: Lesson 4 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: Which box-model property adds space between an element's content and its border?
blocks.explanation: Padding is the space inside the border. Margin is outside the border, while gap controls spacing between items in supported layouts.

blocks.text: PAGE 2 — Build a Complete CSS Website: concepts and applied practice

blocks.title: Lesson 4 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: With box-sizing: border-box, a declared width of 300px generally includes which parts?
options: Padding and margin, but not content
blocks.explanation: The declared width includes content, padding, and border. Margin remains outside that width.

blocks.title: 5. Make Text Easy to Read
blocks.content: Typography affects readability and the website's visual hierarchy. Use a clear heading scale, comfortable line-height, and readable paragraph widths. A design can look impressive but still be difficult to use if the text is too small or cramped. Relative units such as rem are useful for scalable text. Avoid using the same font size and weight for every element.

blocks.title: Create a Readable Text System
blocks.output: Sets readable base typography and fluid heading sizes while preserving line-height for comfortable reading.

blocks.title: Lesson 5 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: What is the main purpose of line-height in text styling?
options: To control the spacing between lines of text
To change the page's background color
To determine the element's border thickness
To position an element at the bottom of the page
blocks.explanation: line-height controls the height of each line box, helping determine the vertical space between lines.

blocks.title: Lesson 5 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: Why might a developer use rem for font sizes?
options: It relates the size to the root element's font size
blocks.explanation: rem is relative to the root element's font size, making it useful for scalable and consistent typography.

blocks.title: 6. Build Navigation with Flexbox
blocks.content: Flexbox is useful for arranging items along a row or column. In our navigation bar, display: flex places the brand and navigation links in a flexible layout. justify-content controls distribution along the main axis, while align-items controls alignment along the cross axis. Use flex-wrap when items may need to move onto another line.

blocks.title: Create a Flexible Navigation Bar
blocks.output: Uses Flexbox alignment, spacing, and wrapping so navigation adapts when there is not enough horizontal space.

blocks.title: Lesson 6 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: Which declaration turns an element into a flex container?
blocks.explanation: display: flex creates a flex container whose direct children become flex items.

blocks.title: Lesson 6 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: Which property creates space between flex items without adding margin to each item?
blocks.explanation: The gap property creates spacing between items in flex and grid layouts.

blocks.title: 7. Arrange Content with CSS Grid
blocks.content: CSS Grid is especially useful for two-dimensional layouts with rows and columns. We will use it to display service cards. The repeat() and minmax() functions help create flexible columns. The auto-fit keyword allows the browser to fit as many columns as the available space permits, while minmax() establishes a minimum and maximum track size.

blocks.title: Create a Responsive Card Grid
blocks.output: Uses CSS Grid auto-fit and minmax to create as many useful columns as the container can fit.

blocks.title: Lesson 7 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: Which layout tool is particularly suited to arranging cards in rows and columns?
blocks.explanation: CSS Grid is designed for two-dimensional layouts, making it well suited to rows and columns of cards.

blocks.title: Lesson 7 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: In grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr), what does 1fr represent?
options: One fraction of the available grid space
blocks.explanation: The fr unit represents a fraction of the available space in the grid container after other track sizing requirements are considered.

blocks.title: 8. Make the Website Responsive
blocks.content: Responsive design lets a website adapt to different screen sizes. Flexible widths, Grid, Flexbox, and media queries work together to make this possible. Start with a layout that works in a narrow viewport, then add breakpoints where the design genuinely needs a change. Do not assume every phone has the same width. Also test long text, large text settings, and touch-friendly controls.

blocks.title: Add a Responsive Breakpoint
blocks.output: Adjusts container and hero spacing on narrow viewports without forcing horizontal scrolling.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Build a Complete CSS Website: concepts and applied practice

blocks.title: Lesson 8 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: What does a media query allow you to do?
options: Apply CSS conditionally, such as when the viewport is within a specified width
Guarantee that a site loads without any network connection
blocks.explanation: Media queries let styles apply when specified conditions are met, including viewport width and user preference settings.

blocks.title: Lesson 8 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: A service-card grid overflows on narrow screens. Which is the best first step?
options: Set every card to a fixed width of 900px
Use flexible grid tracks and test the layout at narrow widths
blocks.explanation: Flexible tracks and narrow-screen testing help the layout adapt instead of forcing content beyond the viewport.

blocks.title: 9. Add Motion Responsibly
blocks.content: Transitions animate changes between CSS states, such as a button's background color on hover. Keyframe animations can create more complex sequences. Motion should support the experience rather than distract from it. Keep animations subtle, avoid animating expensive layout properties unnecessarily, and respect users who prefer reduced motion.

blocks.title: Create a Subtle Interaction
blocks.output: Adds a brief card hover transition and can respect reduced-motion preferences.

blocks.title: Lesson 9 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: Which CSS feature is designed to animate a property change between states?
blocks.explanation: A transition animates changes in supported property values over a specified duration.

blocks.title: Lesson 9 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: Why should a website consider prefers-reduced-motion?
options: It forces every visitor to use dark mode
It allows the design to respect users who request less motion
It removes the need for responsive layouts
blocks.explanation: The prefers-reduced-motion media feature detects a user's motion preference so the site can reduce nonessential animation.

blocks.title: 10. Learn the Professional Details
blocks.content: Good CSS is not only about appearance. It should be predictable, maintainable, and accessible. Use consistent naming, group related styles, avoid unnecessary !important declarations, and remove rules you no longer need. The cascade determines which declarations apply, so inspect specificity and source order before adding more overrides. Use :focus-visible to make keyboard navigation clear. Use semantic HTML, meaningful link text, and sufficient contrast. Finally, check how content behaves when text grows or the viewport changes.

blocks.title: Accessible Focus and Safer Defaults
blocks.output: Improves visible keyboard focus and prevents images from exceeding their containers.

blocks.title: 11. Build the Website — HTML Structure
blocks.content: Create an index.html file. The HTML below supplies the semantic structure for Nova Studio. It links to styles.css, which you will create in the next step. The navigation links point to sections on the same page. The contact link uses an email address placeholder; replace it with a real contact address before publishing. Keep HTML and CSS in separate files so the project remains easier to maintain.

blocks.title: 12. Build the Website — CSS Styling
blocks.content: Create styles.css in the same folder as index.html. This stylesheet uses custom properties, the box model, Flexbox, Grid, responsive rules, focus indicators, and restrained transitions. The design starts with a dark background and purple accent. You can customize the variables later without rewriting the whole stylesheet.

blocks.title: styles.css
blocks.output: Applies the reusable colors, spacing, responsive layout, and interaction styles to the capstone page.

blocks.title: 13. Important CSS Knowledge to Keep
blocks.content: Before finishing, remember these practical rules. First, the cascade decides which declarations apply; if a style does not work, inspect specificity, source order, inheritance, and whether the selector matches. Second, pseudo-classes such as :hover and :focus-visible describe element states, while pseudo-elements such as ::before and ::after style generated content. Third, overflow controls what happens when content exceeds an element's box. Fourth, responsive layouts should be tested at different widths, not just one phone size. Fifth, CSS cannot replace meaningful HTML, keyboard accessibility, or good content. Finally, test your project in a browser and fix real problems instead of adding random overrides.

blocks.title: 14. Test and Finish Your Project
blocks.content: Create both files in the same project folder: index.html and styles.css. Open index.html in a browser. Check that the stylesheet loads, all navigation links reach the correct sections, text remains readable, cards fit narrow screens, and focus indicators appear when using a keyboard. Test the contact link and replace hello@example.com with the correct email address. Inspect the page at more than one viewport width. If you see horizontal scrolling, identify the element causing it rather than hiding the entire problem with overflow-x: hidden. After testing, customize the name, colors, text, and services to make the site your own.

blocks.title: Lesson 10 Review — Question 1 of 2
blocks.question: You change --primary in :root, and several components using var(--primary) update. Why?
options: CSS custom properties allow a shared value to be reused
The browser automatically rewrites every color in the stylesheet
The variable changes all HTML attributes
The :root selector creates a new HTML document
blocks.explanation: The components reference the same custom property, so updating its value changes declarations that use it.

blocks.title: Lesson 10 Review — Question 2 of 2
blocks.question: A link looks attractive but cannot be clearly identified when navigating with a keyboard. What is the best improvement?
options: Remove all outlines so the design looks cleaner
Add a visible :focus-visible style and test keyboard navigation
Replace the link with plain text that cannot be selected
blocks.explanation: A visible focus indicator helps keyboard users identify the element they are navigating to.
